title: HarmoKnight
subtitle: A platform game follows the score
summary: HarmoKnight is Game Freak's Nintendo 3DS rhythm platformer about Tempo, a young hero travelling through the musical world of Melodia. body: HarmoKnight is Game Freak's Nintendo 3DS rhythm platformer about Tempo, a young hero travelling through the musical world of Melodia. Automatically scrolling stages ask him to jump and swing a staff in time with the soundtrack. Enemies and percussion plants become opportunities to add notes to a performance. The simple controls make the connection between music and movement immediately readable. A successful run looks like a small adventure, but its obstacles have been placed so that the player's physical actions can also complete the rhythm of the scene.

Jumping and striking use separate buttons, with the staff also able to charge for a stronger note-earning hit. Routes can contain optional targets and hidden bonuses, giving a skilled player reasons to do more than reach the exit safely. Some stages use different time signatures or changes in speed, asking the hand to adjust to what is heard. The controls remain stable while the musical context changes. That makes a familiar action difficult in another way: the question becomes when to perform it, and how to preserve the phrase through the next obstacle.

Collected notes determine the grade at the end of a stage, and a strong result unlocks a faster version. Boss encounters ask Tempo to answer sequences of actions, while other sections introduce companions with different ways to engage with the music. Bonus stages also use Pokémon melodies, connecting Game Freak's experiment to its better-known work. HarmoKnight builds progression around improved listening. A route first learned as a line of visible hazards can eventually be recognised as a musical pattern, with another speed offering a fresh test of that understanding.
